[S178] Unknown [1225]: Good morning. [S179] Thanks for taking the question. [S180] I guess I had a One question just kind of on the CapEx expectations. [S181] You know, your CapEx as a percentage of revenue has historically been a lot lower than Unifirst has been. [S182] Obviously, you guys are much, much bigger, so that's part of it. [S183] But I guess just philosophically, you know, looking at their assets and the systems to kind of get to CentOS levels. [S184] you know, thinking about, you know, do you expect the CapEx to kind of trend a little bit higher as a percentage of revenue in the first couple of years of integration?
[S185] Scott Garula [1262]: Thank you. [S186] Yeah, Justin, good question. [S187] And I would just say, you know, we just announced the agreement a couple weeks ago. [S188] We'll know a lot more as we close the deal. [S189] But, you know, when we, you know, close this merger, You know, we still expect, you know, not only will we continue to generate strong cash flow, Unifirst generates strong cash flow. [S190] We'll have a strong balance sheet. [S191] You know, we talked on our Unifirst call about, you know, at closing we would expect debt to EBITDA being at [V082] 1.5. [S192] So we're in a great position. [S193] And I don't see our capital allocation priorities really changing. [S194] Our first priority has always been reinvesting back into the business through CapEx, followed by strategic M&A. [S195] And then we'll continue to look at returning capital back to our shareholders in the form of dividends and buybacks. [S196] So more to come on what we would look at in the future with CapEx as a percent of revenue. [S197] as we close the deal. [S198] But I would really not anticipate any material changes in our capital allocation priorities.
[S199] Todd Schneider [1344]: Justin, I'd just like to add to that that, you know, Universe CapEx was higher. [S200] They were certainly trying to catch up on the technology subject and other areas. [S201] And we obviously were in a really good position from a technology footprint. [S202] And we will continue to invest in there because we have to make sure that we're positioned to compete in the marketplace. [S203] That being said, one of the uniquenesses about Uniforce versus most companies that transact like this is they were not for sale. [S204] And as a result, they ran their business very much thinking in the long term. [S205] They invested for the long term. [S206] So we're not Acquiring an asset that needs a significant amount of CapEx investment into facilities and to get it up to standard, they run a really good business. [S207] They think about how to run a business very similar to us. [S208] The cultures are very similar. [S209] They think long term, think about investing for the long term for their people and their customers. [S210] And as a result, we think that positions us incredibly well for the future.
